svg.text: PARAMETERS

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: shared_buffers 8.0 GiB postgresql.shared_buffers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> A quarter of memory is the long-standing starting point, and the cap is the more

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: interesting half of the rule. Past about sixteen gigabytes the operating system

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: page cache is the better place for the memory: it holds the same pages, it can be

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: reclaimed under pressure, and it does not have to be written back through this

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: buffer pool first. A larger number here is a decision about a specific workload

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: rather than a consequence of a larger machine.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: effective_cache_size 24.0 GiB postgresql.effective_cache_size

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Not an allocation, and nothing is reserved by it. It is what the planner is told

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: to assume is cached between the buffer pool and the page cache, and it decides

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: whether an index scan looks cheaper than a sequential one. Set too low, the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: planner avoids indexes it would have read from memory.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: maintenance_work_mem 2.0 GiB postgresql.maintenance_work_mem

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Charged per maintenance operation rather than per connection, and both vacuum and

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: index builds are much faster with room to work in. Capped at two gigabytes

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: because each autovacuum worker takes one of these, so the cost is paid several

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: times over past the point where the return has flattened out.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_connections 100 postgresql.max_connections

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> The upstream default, kept deliberately. Every backend is a process with its own

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: memory, so a larger number here means a larger machine or a smaller work_mem, and

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: neither is free. Past four hundred the answer is a connection pooler rather than

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: a bigger number, which is why that is where the warning sits.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: work_mem 27.0 MiB postgresql.work_mem

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Charged per sort or hash node rather than per connection, and one query can hold

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: several at once, which is what the division by three allows for. It reads

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_connections, so the two are computed in that order however they are written

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: here. This is the parameter that turns a busy afternoon into an out-of-memory

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: kill, and it is sized to be survivable rather than fast.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: wal_buffers 16.0 MiB postgresql.wal_buffers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: held at its maximum

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> A thirty-second of the buffer pool, capped where PostgreSQL's own automatic

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: setting stops. Beyond one log segment there is nothing further to buffer: the log

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: is written and flushed on commit either way.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: min_wal_size 1.0 GiB postgresql.min_wal_size

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> The floor the log is allowed to shrink back to. Recycling segments already on

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: disk costs nothing; creating them again during the next burst costs a write per

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: segment, at the worst possible moment.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_wal_size 4.0 GiB postgresql.max_wal_size

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> How much log may accumulate before a checkpoint is forced. Larger means fewer

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: checkpoints and less write amplification, and a longer recovery after a crash.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: Four gigabytes is roughly where most workloads stop noticing either, and it is

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: what the free space floor on the wal path is set to cover several times over.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: checkpoint_completion_target

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: 0.9 postgresql.checkpoint_completion_target

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Spread a checkpoint's writes across nine tenths of the interval rather than

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: issuing them as fast as the disk will take them. The alternative is a periodic

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: stall that shows up in commit latency and nowhere else, which is very hard to

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: explain to whoever reports it.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_worker_processes 8 postgresql.max_worker_processes

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> One per core above eight, and the upstream default of eight below that: a small

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: machine is not improved by having fewer background workers than PostgreSQL

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: assumes it has. This is a ceiling on processes rather than a reservation of them.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_parallel_workers 8 postgresql.max_parallel_workers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Every parallel worker comes out of the pool above, so allowing more of them than

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: exist would be a number that means nothing. They are kept equal by reading it, so

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: that the relationship is visible in the plan rather than implied by two numbers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: that happen to match.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_parallel_workers_per_gather

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: 4 postgresql.max_parallel_workers_per_gather

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Half the cores, so one large query cannot take the whole machine and leave every

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: other connection queued behind it. Capped at eight because past that the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: coordination between workers costs more than the parallelism returns on anything

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: but a pure scan.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: max_parallel_maintenance_workers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: 2 postgresql.max_parallel_maintenance_workers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Index builds parallelise well and are usually run while something else is using

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: the machine, so this is deliberately smaller than the per-query limit. Each

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: worker also takes its own maintenance_work_mem, which is the real reason for the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: cap.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: autovacuum_max_workers 3 postgresql.autovacuum_max_workers

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: raised to its minimum

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> Three is the upstream default and is enough for a small machine. More cores

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: usually means more tables written to at once, and autovacuum falling behind is

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: the failure that stays invisible until the day a table is twice the size it

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: should be.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: random_page_cost 1.1 postgresql.random_page_cost

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> On solid state storage a random read costs very nearly what a sequential one

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: does, and a planner told otherwise avoids indexes it should be using. Four is the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: upstream default and is written for a disk with a seek to pay for. This is the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: one parameter here whose right answer is a property of the hardware rather than

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: of the workload.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: effective_io_concurrency 200 postgresql.effective_io_concurrency

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> How many reads the storage can usefully have in flight at once, which is what a

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: bitmap heap scan uses to decide how far ahead to prefetch. Two hundred describes

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: a device that queues internally; two describes a device with one arm.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: default_statistics_target 100 postgresql.default_statistics_target

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: -> The upstream default, here to be visible rather than to be changed. Raising it is

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: a per-column decision taken after a bad plan has been diagnosed, not something to

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

svg.text: do to every column of every table in advance.
